documents.title: Acute Visit — Loose Stools
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit, called this morning.

About a week of loose stools, 3-4 a day, pale and greasy, hard to flush, with a bad smell. No blood or black stool. No fever. No vomiting. No recent travel, no sick contacts, no antibiotics. Appetite normal, eating as usual. He thinks he has lost weight over the past month; his belt is a notch tighter. Some upper abdominal ache on and off, like the bouts he has had over the years, nothing severe.

Exam: BP 120/71, HR 74, T 36.5, SpO2 99%. Wt 76.8 kg (79.6 kg on 1/19). Not jaundiced. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding, no masses, no organomegaly. Bowel sounds normal.

A/P:
Greasy loose stools with weight loss in a man with a history of heavy drinking, bouts of upper abdominal pain over the years, and a brother with chronic pancreatitis. Malabsorption from the pancreas is the main concern. Referred to GI, asked for an early appointment; GI office will arrange stool testing and imaging as they see fit.
- Fluids, regular meals.
- Return or call for fever, blood in stool, vomiting, severe pain.
- Glucose: no lows; continue glargine.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST
Indication: steatorrhea, weight loss, intermittent upper abdominal pain.
Findings:
Pancreas: diffuse parenchymal atrophy with multiple coarse calcifications throughout the head, body and tail. The main pancreatic duct is irregularly dilated with beaded contour, and side branches are dilated. No focal mass. No peripancreatic fluid collection or inflammatory stranding.
Liver: normal size, smooth contour, no focal lesion. Patent portal vein. No ascites.
Gallbladder surgically absent. No biliary dilatation.
Spleen, adrenals: normal. Kidneys: normal size, no hydronephrosis or stones.
Bowel: no obstruction or wall thickening. Appendix surgically absent.
Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: Findings of chronic pancreatitis: atrophy, coarse calcifications and irregularly dilated pancreatic ducts. No mass or acute inflammation.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 02/24/2021
Referred by: primary care, for greasy stools and weight loss.

HPI: 56-year-old man with untreated hepatitis C and insulin-treated diabetes. For the last three weeks his stools have been loose, bulky and foul, and he notices an oily sheen left on the water. Over the past month he has lost weight without trying, although he is eating as much as ever. No fever, no blood per rectum, no travel. He describes upper abdominal pain that has come and gone for years. He drinks now and then and says he has cut back a lot over the past year.

PMH: chronic hepatitis C (about 2006, untreated); diabetes on basal insulin.
PSH: appendectomy (age 12), cholecystectomy (age 45).
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: brother with chronic pancreatitis; father with alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis; mother with type 2 diabetes.
SH: former smoker, 30 pack-years. Alcohol as above.

Exam: comfortable. No jaundice. No palmar erythema, spider nevi or other cutaneous signs of chronic liver disease seen. Abdomen soft, mildly tender in the epigastrium, no guarding or rebound, no palpable mass.

Labs today: Hgb 12.6, MCV 92, platelets 167. Albumin 3.2 (low). AST 78, ALT 59, bilirubin 0.9, creatinine 0.9.
CT abdomen/pelvis today: atrophic pancreas with coarse calcification and irregular ductal dilation; liver without focal lesion.

Assessment:
1. Chronic pancreatitis with exocrine pancreatic insufficiency. The CT is diagnostic and the steatorrhea with weight loss reflects exocrine failure. Alcohol and family history both likely contribute.
2. Diabetes: in light of chronic calcific pancreatitis, his insulin-requiring diabetes is best classified as diabetes secondary to chronic pancreatitis (type 3c, pancreatogenic). Continue current insulin through primary care.
3. Mild anemia and low albumin, likely nutritional in the setting of malabsorption.
4. Chronic hepatitis C, followed by primary care.

Plan:
- Start pancrelipase (Creon) 36,000 lipase units by mouth with each meal and each snack, taken with the first bites. Prescription sent.
- Complete alcohol abstinence advised strongly; he agreed to stop.
- Weight and stool response at follow-up; primary care to monitor weight, albumin and glucose.

Thank you for involving us.
Gastroenterology

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is great news on both counts, and stopping drinking is the best thing you can do for your pancreas and your liver. Keep taking the Creon with every meal and every snack. Watch your sugars: as you absorb food better they can run a little higher, and let me know if you see any lows. Let's see you in late May. If cravings or withdrawal symptoms come up, call me, we have options.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up: chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency, hepatitis C, type 3c diabetes. First visit since GI consult in February.

Interval: GI diagnosed chronic calcific pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency, started Creon 36,000 units with meals and snacks. Diabetes now classified as type 3c (pancreatogenic). He stopped drinking in late February and has stayed sober, about 3 months.

Today: mild fatigue for a few weeks, "just run down." Weight steady since February. No heat intolerance, no palpitations, no tremor. Stools formed, 1-2 a day on Creon. Eating well. No abdominal pain bouts since February. No confusion, no bleeding.
Medication review: Creon 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime. No thyroid medicine, no steroids, no testosterone or other hormones, no supplements.
Sugars: fasting 100-140, no lows.

Exam: BP 118/77, HR 84, T 36.6, SpO2 98%, Wt 77.9 kg.
General: thin face with temporal muscle wasting.
Skin: several spider angiomas over the upper chest. No jaundice.
Neck: thyroid not enlarged, nontender, no nodules.
Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abdomen: distended, nontender, positive fluid wave. No palpable spleen.
Extremities: mild pitting edema at both ankles.

A/P:
1. Chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency: good response to Creon. Continue 36,000 units with meals and snacks.
2. Chronic hepatitis C: exam with temporal wasting, spider angiomas on upper chest, mild ankle edema and a fluid wave. CMP, CBC and INR today.
3. Hypoalbuminemia: albumin 3.2 at GI in February. Adding to problem list. Recheck today.
4. Anemia, mild: Hgb 12.6 in February, down from 14s. CBC today.
5. Type 3c diabetes: continue glargine 24 units. A1c today.
6. Fatigue: thyroid tests today along with the above.
7. Alcohol use disorder, early remission: sober since February. Strongly supported; he is not interested in a program right now, feels he does not need one.

Follow up in 3 months.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Albumin 3.1, AST 82, ALT 64, bilirubin 1.0, INR 1.1. Hgb 12.5, MCV 92, platelets 163. A1c 6.7.
Thyroid: TSH 2.3 and free T4 1.1, both normal. Total T4 4.2 ug/dL (send-out), low.
Reads as euthyroid. The low total T4 with normal TSH and free T4 fits low binding protein, in keeping with his low albumin and liver disease. No thyroid treatment needed. Will message patient.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Mike,

Your thyroid is working normally. One of the thyroid numbers (total T4) came back low, but that test depends on proteins in the blood that carry the hormone, and those are low for you right now along with your albumin. The tests that actually reflect thyroid function, TSH and free T4, are normal. No treatment needed.

Albumin is 3.1, a bit lower than February, and the liver enzymes are about where they have been. Blood count is mildly low but steady. A1c 6.7.

Keep up the Creon, the food and the sobriety. See you in August.

events.reason: Dizziness, palpitations and sweating before meals

documents.title: Emergency Department Visit
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 08/23/2021
(Record forwarded to primary care 08/26/2021 after final labs posted.)

Chief complaint: dizzy spells before meals.

HPI: 57-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis and exocrine insufficiency, type 3c diabetes on basal insulin, previously worked up for malabsorption and low albumin. Over the past few weeks he has had episodes of lightheadedness, a racing heartbeat and sweating that come on before meals, especially late morning when breakfast is small, and go away once he eats. This morning had a spell while doing yard work and came in. No loss of consciousness, no chest pain, no focal weakness.

PMH: chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency; type 3c diabetes; chronic hepatitis C; low albumin.
PSH: appendectomy; cholecystectomy.
Meds: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, 30 pack-years. Alcohol use disorder, no alcohol since February 2021.

Vitals: BP 124/76, HR 88, RR 16, T 36.7, SpO2 98% on arrival; stable throughout.
Exam: alert, comfortable after juice. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Neuro nonfocal. No remarkable findings.

Results:
- Fasting glucose 60 mg/dL on arrival (before oral glucose).
- Hemoglobin A1c 6.2%.
- C-peptide 0.5 ng/mL (reference 1.1-4.4), low. Resulted 08/25.
- Serum insulin: reported low. Resulted 08/25. Note: this insulin immunoassay may not detect glargine, so a low result does not exclude exogenous basal insulin.

ED course: given oral glucose and a meal; repeat fingerstick normal. Observed several hours without recurrence.

Assessment: insulin-induced hypoglycemia. Low glucose on basal insulin with a low C-peptide, so no excess of his own insulin; fits glargine acting during long gaps between meals.

Disposition: discharged home.
- Eat regular meals and snacks; do not skip breakfast. Take Creon with each.
- Check glucose before meals and with any symptoms; treat under 70 with 15 g fast sugar.
- Insulin glargine dose not changed at discharge (24 units).
- Follow up with primary care within 1 week.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called patient after ED notification 8/23 (hypoglycemia). Feels fine. No further spells since. Eating breakfast and a mid-morning snack, Creon with both. Checking sugars before meals, 90s-130s. Knows to treat a low with juice or glucose tabs and recheck. Follow-up booked 8/30 with PCP.

documents.title: Acute Visit — Fatigue and Bruising
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Was due for routine follow-up; moved up because of symptoms.

HPI: over about 6 months he has gotten steadily more tired, now napping most afternoons. Bruises on his forearms and shins from minor bumps. Weight down a few kilos without trying. Eating well, taking Creon with all meals and snacks, stools formed. No fever, no night sweats. No lumps he has noticed. No bleeding gums, no blood in stool or urine. Still sober, about a year now. No new medicines.
Glucose: no lows, fasting 100s-130s.

Exam: BP 138/74, HR 71, T 36.6, SpO2 98%, Wt 73.0 kg (76.7 kg in October).
Scattered ecchymoses on both forearms and shins, no petechiae.
No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy.
Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, spleen tip palpable below the left costal margin on inspiration. Liver edge not palpable. No fluid wave today.
Spider angiomas on chest unchanged. Temporal wasting. Trace ankle edema.

A/P:
1. Fatigue, easy bruising, weight loss with a palpable spleen: CBC with differential and CMP today, stat.
2. Pancreatic insufficiency, type 3c diabetes, hepatitis C: unchanged regimen.
Will call with results today or tomorrow.

Addendum 16:30: CBC back. WBC 11.8 with lymphocytes 64%, hemoglobin 10.1, MCV 96, platelets 82. Bicytopenia with lymphocytosis and splenomegaly. Urgent hematology-oncology referral placed and called to their office; request smear review. Albumin 3.2, AST 83, ALT 60.

documents.title: Call with blood count results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called patient. Explained the low hemoglobin and platelets, the high lymphocyte count and the enlarged spleen, and that these need a blood specialist to look at the cells and possibly the bone marrow. Hematology has an opening 3/7, booked. Bleeding and infection precautions reviewed: avoid aspirin and NSAIDs, call for fever over 38.0, any bleeding that won't stop, black stools. He asked if this is from his liver; told him it could contribute but the pattern needs hematology. He understands.

reports.text:
BONE MARROW ASPIRATE AND CORE BIOPSY, POSTERIOR ILIAC CREST
Clinical: anemia, thrombocytopenia and lymphocytosis with splenomegaly; peripheral smear with hairy cytoplasmic projections.
Core biopsy: marrow infiltrated by small to intermediate atypical lymphoid cells with oval nuclei and moderate pale cytoplasm.
Special stains: atypical lymphoid cells are positive for tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP).
reports.conclusion: Bone marrow infiltrated by TRAP-positive atypical lymphoid cells, consistent with hairy cell leukemia.

documents.title: Hematology-Oncology Consultation
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY-ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit date: 03/07/2022
Reason for referral: anemia, thrombocytopenia, lymphocytosis and splenomegaly.

HPI: 57-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis and exocrine insufficiency, type 3c diabetes, chronic hepatitis C, low albumin and a hypoglycemic episode last August. He reports half a year of mounting tiredness, bruising easily, and about 10 lb of weight loss without trying. No fevers. No drenching sweats at night. He has not felt any enlarged glands.

Medications: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: appendectomy, cholecystectomy.
FH: father alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis (died 65); mother type 2 diabetes; brother chronic pancreatitis.
SH: former construction supervisor on disability. Former smoker, 30 pack-years. Alcohol use disorder, abstinent about a year.

Exam: spleen markedly enlarged, palpable well below the left costal margin. Liver not enlarged. No palpable lymph nodes in cervical, axillary or inguinal regions.

Labs today: WBC 12.0; differential lymphocytes 60%, basophils 2%, eosinophils 3%, monocytes 5%, neutrophils 30%. Hemoglobin 10.0. Platelets 80. Reticulocytes 1%.
Peripheral smear (reviewed personally): atypical lymphocytes with hair-like cytoplasmic projections.
Bone marrow biopsy today: marrow infiltrated by atypical lymphoid cells that are TRAP positive (report finalized 03/10).

Assessment: hairy cell leukemia.

Plan:
- Cladribine, a single 5-day IV course, 03/21 to 03/25/2022.
- Counts weekly during recovery; transfusion support if needed.
- Infection precautions reviewed; he should call for any fever.
- Return 4 months after treatment for response assessment.

We appreciate the referral and will keep you updated.
Hematology-Oncology

documents.title: Feeling wiped out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the leukemia treatment last week. Really wiped out and my sugar has been running a little higher, 140s-150s in the morning. No fever. Is that normal or should I come in?

documents.title: RE: Feeling wiped out
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Fatigue for several weeks after cladribine is expected while your counts recover. Morning sugars in the 140s-150s are fine for now; I would rather you run a bit high than low. Keep eating regular meals and snacks with your Creon. If you get a fever of 100.4 or more, call the oncology office right away. Let's plan to see you in June.

documents.title: Hematology-Oncology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Dunn on 07/12/2022, about 4 months after cladribine for hairy cell leukemia.

He feels well, with energy close to his baseline and no infections. Exam: spleen tip barely palpable, much reduced from March. No lymphadenopathy.
CBC today shows recovered counts, and no hairy cells are seen on the smear.

Impression: hairy cell leukemia in remission after one course of cladribine, with recovered blood counts and a regressing spleen.

Plan: surveillance with CBC and exam every 6 months; next visit February 2023. Please let us know of any recurrent cytopenias, fevers or abdominal fullness.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications unchanged (pancrelipase, insulin glargine).

Hematology-Oncology
